work-interval.short: The hard part of an interval session: each bout of effort, set by how hard it is and how long it lasts.

relief-interval.short: The recovery between two work intervals: rest or easy exercise, set by how long it lasts and how easy it is.

sprint-interval-training.short: Intervals of all-out sprints, usually 30 s or shorter, harder than the power that draws out VO₂max, each followed by a long easy recovery of a few minutes.

vvo2max.short: The lowest running speed at which VO₂max is reached in a ramp test: the running version of maximal aerobic power.

threshold-interval.short: Long work intervals, about 8–20 min each, at an intensity close to critical power or the second threshold: hard, but well below VO₂max power.

time-at-vo2max.short: How long a session keeps oxygen uptake at or near VO₂max, usually counted as the time above 90% of VO₂max.

mitochondrial-biogenesis.short: The building of new mitochondria, and the growth of existing ones, inside muscle fibres: the muscle's response to the stress of training.

microcycle.short: A short unit of a training plan, usually one week, sometimes a few days.

block-periodisation.short: Packing hard sessions into a short, concentrated block (for example five interval sessions in one week), then training lightly, instead of spreading them evenly.

functional-overreaching.short: A short, planned dip in performance after a hard block of training that turns into a gain once the athlete has recovered, within days to a couple of weeks.

nonfunctional-overreaching.short: A dip in performance from too much training and too little recovery that lasts weeks to months and brings no extra gain afterwards.

overtraining-syndrome.short: A drop in performance lasting months or longer, from too much load and too little recovery, often with fatigue and low mood. Found by ruling out other causes such as illness.

training-status.short: How trained a person already is: untrained, active, trained or elite. The more trained, the smaller the gain from the same training.

time-trial.short: A race or test against the clock over a set distance, done alone, as fast as possible. Used in studies as a measure of endurance performance.
